title: UbuntuGuard device inventory report, version 1
description: Full-replace inventory sent by the agent. Everything here is DISCOVERED at runtime, never hardcoded. The platform-neutral fields are the ones the server reasons about; anything adapter-specific lives under adapter.details, which the server stores and displays but never interprets. That is what keeps the server free of Ubuntu-specific logic while still surfacing Ubuntu facts in the dashboard.

release_build.description: False means dev-only environment overrides are compiled in. The dashboard flags such devices, because their effective settings may not match policy.

boot_id.description: Changes every boot; lets the server distinguish a reboot from a restart.

machine_id_hash.description: SHA-256 of /etc/machine-id, hashed on the agent. The raw value is never transmitted.

virtualization.description: Hypervisor name or 'none'. Used as a clone-detection signal.

network_interfaces.description: Standard IT inventory. Loopback and virtual interfaces are excluded. Note the contrast with enrollment, which sends only hashed MACs for clone fingerprinting.

detail.description: Human-readable reason when supported is false, e.g. 'usbguard not installed'. Drives the 'unsupported' status in the dashboard instead of a misleading green tick.

capabilities.description: What this device can actually do. A policy targeting a capability reported unsupported resolves to status 'unsupported', never 'applied'.

name.description: OS adapter identity, e.g. 'ubuntu'. The server treats this as an opaque label.

details.description: Flat adapter-specific key/value facts, e.g. usbguard_version, usbguard_daemon_active, usbguard_dbus_available, usbguard_rules_path. Deliberately flat and scalar-valued: the server stores and renders it without interpretation, so adding a macOS or Windows adapter later requires no server change.

applied_policies.description: What the agent believes is actually enforced, as confirmed by reading real OS state back, not by a successful exit code.
